correctness.rationale: A specified unordered pair of labels is a cherry in (2n-5)!! of (2n-3)!! PDA trees; contraction bijectively produces a uniformly sampled (n-1)-leaf tree with a marked surrogate leaf. Re-expansion changes S by d+2, so counting all binom(n,2) marked pairs gives the equality for every test function without falsely asserting D independent of S. Randomizing child orientation gives uniform Catalan full binary plane shapes; weighted recursion B=2TB+2xTT' gives mean Sackin n(q_n-1). The f(s)=s identity and E[D|tree]=S/(n-1) yield the exact covariance; the ratio a_(n+1)/a_n=1+(n-2)/(n(2n-1)) proves zero boundaries and strict negativity. Stirling central-binomial asymptotic gives coefficient -sqrt(pi)/8. Independently enumerated all Catalan plane trees n=2..9 and compared the full size-biased distribution and moments; those cases corroborate the all-size bijection.

value.rationale: Cherries measure local branching and Sackin global path length, widely used complementary phylogenetic balance statistics under the PDA null model. The identity transfers an entire size-biased distribution and yields a nonobvious all-size sign and sharp scaling that neither marginal mean determines, a natural dependency calculation.

final_claim: For uniform rooted binary nonplane leaf-labeled phylogenetic (PDA) trees, cherry-marked Sackin size bias satisfies E[C_n f(S_n)]=n(n-1)/(2(2n-3))*E[f(S_{n-1}+D_{n-1}+2)] with D a uniformly selected leaf depth conditional on that very same smaller tree. Cov(C_n,S_n)=n*(4(n-1)-n q_n)/(4(2n-3)), q_n=4^(n-1)/binom(2n-2,n-1), zero at n=2,3, negative for n>=4 and asymptotic -sqrt(pi)*n^(3/2)/8.
limitations: Uniform labeled nonplane rooted PDA trees; not the Yule/Kingman distribution, unlabeled uniform tree shapes or nonbinary phylogenies.
No negative-association claim, monotone Sackin regression on cherry counts or joint limit theorem.
Finite Catalan enumerations through nine leaves support but do not replace the all-n bijection and algebra.
